annotations.annotation_text: Page 593 opens Book 4, Chapter 1 ("The Ricorso — Dawn") during the Ricorso (The Return) phase. This passage continues dawn breaking over Dublin Bay, St. Kevin bathing at Glendalough, St. Patrick vs. the Archdruid Balkelly, ALP's dissolving final monologue into the sea, featuring St. Kevin, St. Patrick, Balkelly, ALP. The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.

annotations.annotation_text: Cosmic dawn chant (593.01): Sanskrit 'sandhyā' (twilight, the sacred junction between night and morning / Hindu dawn prayer) fused with Catholic liturgical chant 'Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus', opening the ricorso.
sources: Campbell, Joseph and Robinson, Henry Morton. A Skeleton Key. https://archive.org/details/skeletonkeytofin00camp
Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic node on page 593 ("The Ricorso — Dawn"): Joyce weaves multilingual puns across 60+ languages — etymological roots from the Contemporary Literature Press lexicons (Romanian, Scandinavian, Slavic, Classical) intersect with local Dublin speech rhythms. The Ricorso (The Return) dream-logic transforms ordinary syntax into a palimpsest of global literary and mythic references.
sources: Tindall, William York. A Reader's Guide to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/readersguidetofi00tind
Contemporary Literature Press: Multilingual Lexicons for FW. https://editura.mttlc.ro

annotations.annotation_text: Solar boustrophedon "Pu Nuseht" (593.10): "The Sun Up" written in reverse mirror-spelling, representing the solar disc bursting over Howth Head and dispersing the nocturnal dream-shadows.

Oneiric dimension "night" on page 593 ("The Ricorso — Dawn"): the nocturnal consciousness surfaces within dawn breaking over Dublin Bay, St. Kevin bathing at Glendalough, St. Patrick vs. the Archdruid Balkelly, ALP's dissolving final monologue into the sea. During this Ricorso (The Return) phase, Joyce reconstructs the sleeping body's sensory deprivation — dimmed sight, distorted hearing, dream-logic association — transforming somatic experience into polyphonic language.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Freud, Sigmund. The Interpretation of Dreams. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/4349
Troy, Mark L. Mummeries of Resurrection. http://www.rosenlake.net

annotations.annotation_text: Egyptian Book of the Dead title (593.20): Book IV corresponds to the ancient Egyptian funerary papyrus title 'Rāu nu pert em hru' (Chapters of Coming Forth by Day), signaling spiritual resurrection.
sources: Budge, E.A. Wallis. The Book of the Dead. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/1300
